You have now written all three specification styles. Each suits a different job:

- **Keyword-driven** — the default. Tests are sequences of keyword calls. Use it
  for most work; it is the most flexible.
- **Behavior-driven** — keyword calls prefixed with `Given`/`When`/`Then` so a
  test reads as a sentence. Use it when non-engineers read or write the tests,
  or when the behavior is the specification.
- **Data-driven** — a template run once per data row. Use it when one action is
  checked against many input/expected pairs; it removes repetition.

These are not exclusive. A suite can be mostly keyword-driven with one templated
data table, and a behavior-driven test can call templated keywords underneath.
Choose the style that makes each test easiest to read and to change.

> **Tip:** When a suite starts to repeat itself row after row, that is the
> signal to reach for a template. When stakeholders need to read the tests,
> reach for behavior-driven phrasing.
